events.title: Born in Launceston
events.text: Born in Launceston, Tasmania.

events.title: Tasmania debut at 17
events.text: First-class debut for Tasmania aged 17 years and 337 days, the youngest Tasmanian to play in the Sheffield Shield.

events.title: ODI debut
events.text: First one-day international, against South Africa in a four-team tournament in New Zealand.

events.title: Test debut
events.text: First Test, against Sri Lanka.

events.title: World Cup hundred in Jaipur
events.text: A century against the West Indies makes him, at the time, the youngest batter to score a World Cup hundred.

events.title: First World Cup
events.text: A World Cup winner for the first time, as a player.

events.title: One-day captain
events.text: Takes over the captaincy of the one-day side.

events.title: World Cup won as captain
events.text: Australia win every match of the tournament. Ponting makes an unbeaten hundred in the final against India.

events.title: Test captain
events.text: Succeeds Steve Waugh as Australia's Test captain.

events.title: The Ashes lost in England
events.text: Australia lose an Ashes series for the first time since 1987.

events.title: Champions Trophy
events.text: Australia win the Champions Trophy for the first time, in India.

events.title: The Ashes regained
events.text: A clean sweep at home. Ponting is player of the series and wins the Compton–Miller Medal.

events.title: Second World Cup as captain
events.text: Unbeaten through the tournament again, this time in the West Indies. He is the ICC's Cricketer of the Year for the second year running.

events.title: Steps away from T20 internationals
events.text: Retires from Twenty20 internationals to prolong his career in the longer formats.

events.title: Hands over the captaincy
events.text: Resigns as captain after the World Cup and plays on under Michael Clarke.

events.title: Officer of the Order of Australia
events.text: Appointed on Australia Day for services to cricket and, through the Ponting Foundation, the community.

events.title: Last Test
events.text: Announces his retirement on 29 November and plays his final Test against South Africa in Perth.

events.title: Last season as a player
events.text: Captains Mumbai Indians in the IPL, plays county cricket for Surrey, and is named Sheffield Shield Player of the Year for 2012–13.

events.title: Head coach, Mumbai Indians
events.text: Named head coach in December 2014. Mumbai win the IPL the following season.

events.title: Head coach, Delhi
events.text: Appointed by Delhi Daredevils, who become Delhi Capitals the next year.

events.title: ICC Hall of Fame
events.text: Inducted into the ICC Cricket Hall of Fame. The Australian Cricket Hall of Fame follows in the same year.

events.title: Delhi reach the IPL final
events.text: Delhi Capitals finish as runners-up, their first final.

events.title: Head coach, Washington Freedom
events.text: Appointed for the second season of Major League Cricket. The side wins the title that year.

events.title: Head coach, Punjab Kings
events.text: Appointed in September 2024. In his first season Punjab top the league table and reach the final.
